key_decisions.decision: Keeps ish ish as any man and renders the contextual flesh euphemism explicitly; avoids calling the discharge gonorrhea or equating it with the semen case later.
Follows the pinned Masoretic wording, retaining both flowing and blockage; records the longer ancient reading in a note instead of importing it silently.
Reads flesh here as the body generally rather than narrowing contact to the genitals, with the repeated washing formula intact.
Keeps merkav broader than a saddle so other riding supports are not excluded by a narrow equipment choice.
Preserves the difference between touching and carrying, and does not add clothes washing to the shorter first clause.
Makes clear whose hands are unwashed and who must bathe; does not claim rinsing the man's hands cures or ends the discharge.
Makes cessation distinct from completed ritual cleanness and preserves the special living-water requirement and seven days.
Preserves distinct offering roles and discharge as the stated occasion for atonement; does not add a sin or a forgiveness formula.
Names semen plainly, retains whole-body washing and evening, and treats this as a separate case from the earlier discharge.
Keeps the sexual relation, emission and plural bathing/status requirements without adding marital status or moral disapproval.
Preserves the woman's seven-day interval and the contact person's evening interval as different durations; no exile rule is added.
Takes ambiguous hu as an object lying on the bed or seat; the alternative that it resumes the bed or seat itself is noted rather than concealed.
Preserves intercourse, transferred impurity, seven days and bedding consequences; does not harmonize this case with later prohibitions by inventing accidental onset.
Preserves both prolonged bleeding outside the usual time and bleeding extending beyond it, without assigning a cause.
Distinguishes cessation from the following count and clean result; does not import an unstated bathing requirement from the male rule.
Keeps both offering roles and the source's discharge-impurity relation without adding personal wrongdoing or forgiveness.
Preserves the address to the two leaders, death warning and divine dwelling among the people; does not add an unspecified physical separation policy.
Keeps menstruation, both sexes with discharges and the intercourse case; menstrual wording renders the contextual davah without making a modern illness diagnosis.
